sourceInformation.tech: Three.js r180 (0.180.0), WebGPURenderer, TSL; Rapier 0.19.3; Gamepad API; Web Audio; WebRTC; AI Hub Session Protocol v1 client 1.4.0
sourceInformation.artDirection: Procedural cel shading, ink silhouettes, faceted terrain, warm paper UI, turquoise water and signal-yellow aircraft
sourceInformation.animation: Three.js AnimationMixer and AnimationClip keyframes for propellers, rotors and barrel rolls; procedural banking, floating, wakes and particle motion
sourceInformation.audio: Code-generated electronic music at 10% default volume, synthesized effects and Animalese-style gibberish radio; no audio files
sourceInformation.online: 1–4 shared-world co-op through AI Hub; standalone direct WebRTC radio-code invitations; 1–4 couch co-op
sourceInformation.testing: Headless Chromium, WebGPU software adapter, WebGL2 compatibility, simulated standard gamepads, emulated touch, audio analyser, full scripted mission and AI Hub harness. Physical controllers, real phones, audibility and public-internet connectivity unknown.
sourceInformation.research: No internet research. Native model knowledge of the source; supplied AI Hub integration files and installed dependency source read for implementation.

testingFeedback: Testing caught five game issues: an obsolete physics-module import, a clipped phone sector banner, flagship camera/HUD framing, fast remote action taps being missed, and a waiting overlay blocking a disconnect debrief. All were fixed. Test assertions also needed corrections for fuel-station overlap, floating-point gain precision, attract timing and the source-field count.
One was game breaking: the physics-module 404 prevented startup.

The full fixed-step browser playthrough proved both bridges, refueling, rolls, bursts, all three sectors and the flagship could reach victory. Two-page WebRTC tests caught transient-input and disconnect recovery bugs; the official Hub harness verified the session lifecycle.
WebGPU screenshots were least helpful because the headless WebGPU canvas was blank; state checks verified that backend and WebGL2 screenshots supplied the visual checks.
engineFeedback: Three.js let the procedural geometry, ink silhouettes, stepped TSL shading and native animation clips share one scene across WebGPU and the compatibility backend.

I initially used an obsolete Rapier module filename; inspecting the installed 0.19.3 package fixed it. Screenshot review also exposed a camera/encounter framing mistake that simulation-only assertions missed.
The complete river-flight simulation, enemy patterns, fuel economy, UI focus/input system and host-authoritative co-op protocol.
Coordinating the asynchronous renderer, sensor-based physics, frame timing and multiple networked copies.
A built-in controller-first UI focus system and a unified deterministic simulation/network clock would simplify small arcade games.
promptFeedback: The source, procedural-audio rule and TV/controller-first requirement gave the game a clear identity.
The ban on internet research and the required online integration overlap; I treated the supplied protocol as implementation material and did no source research.
Making a complete solo, couch and networked sortie work inside a single shareable HTML file while keeping all menus usable with a controller.
State whether standalone online play may use a hosted signaling service; direct code exchange is portable but adds a connection step.

aiHub.name: Stream Scheme
aiHub.description: A cel-ink river shooter with a very questionable flight plan. Skim branching channels, steal fuel, smash bridges and sink the Tax Collector solo or with a wing of friends.
aiHub.controls: WASD/arrows or left stick: fly/throttle; Space/click or Cross/RT: fire; Shift/right click or Circle/RB: roll; E or Square/LT: burst; Esc/Options: pause. Touch: drag to fly, auto aim/fire, tap right to roll, double tap for burst.
